steps.body: The split can be WRITTEN: 15 = 10 + 5. The equals sign says both sides name one amount: teen, and ten-and-ones.
steps.narration: The split can be WRITTEN: 15 = 10 + 5. The equals sign says both sides name one amount: teen, and ten-and-ones.

widget.prompt: A full group of 10 is already shown. Add the extra dots needed to make 14.

commonCounts.feedback: 0 leaves 4 dots still missing — the ten alone only makes 10, not 14.
3 leaves 1 dot still missing; ten and 3 is 13, one short of 14.
5 adds 1 too many; ten and 5 is 15, one past 14.

widget.missFeedback: The ten is done; count on from 10 while adding dots, and stop when you reach 14.
widget.successFeedback: 14 built — one complete ten and 4 more, exactly what the teen numeral says.

predict.prompt: Which equation matches a full ten and 4 more?
predict.reveal: The left digit of 14 is a whole ten, so the true equation adds 10, not 1.

cml.actionGoal: Build one complete ten, then count on the ones, for knb teen equation.
invariants: Every teen number is one complete ten and some ones — the left digit records the finished ten, the right digit counts the extras — and that split is what knb teen equation rests on.
misconceptions: Reading the 1 of a teen as “one” instead of one TEN, or counting only the leftover ones and forgetting the completed ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more dot joined the ones, which teen would the frame show then?

widget.prompt: Which equation tells the truth about 15?

options.feedback: 5 + 5 makes 10; the equation for fifteen needs the whole ten plus five more.
That reads backwards — the two parts stand left of the equals, the whole on the right.
That treats the 1 of 15 as one; the left digit is a full ten, so the sum is 10 + 5.
Correct — fifteen is one complete ten and five ones, and the equation says exactly that.

widget.prompt: Start at 10 and count on 3. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 12 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 13.
14 goes one complete hop too far. Count just 3 hops from 10 to land on 13.

widget.missFeedback: Count 3 on from 10: you land on 13.
widget.successFeedback: 10 and 3 more is 13 — the teen numeral written as a walk: ten first, then the ones.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — all 3 counts past ten are needed to reach 13.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — the count-on stops after 3 numbers, on 13.

widget.prompt: Which pair is NOT a split of 14?

options.label: 10 and 4
options.feedback: 10 + 4 = 14, so this pair is a valid split of 14 — the teen split itself.

options.label: 14 and 0
options.feedback: 14 + 0 = 14, so this pair is a valid split of 14, keeping everything in one part.

options.label: 10 and 5
options.feedback: Correct — 10 + 5 = 15, one too many, so this pair is not a split of 14.

options.label: 13 and 1
options.feedback: 13 + 1 = 14, so this pair is a valid split of 14.
